nahhas-irab:72-72.t: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): the ism (noun) of inna. (وَالَّذِينَ آوَوْا وَنَصَرُوا): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to it. (أُولئِكَ): nominative (marfūʿ) as a mubtadaʾ (subject); (بَعْضُهُمْ): a second mubtadaʾ; (أَوْلِياءُ بَعْضٍ): its khabar (predicate), and the whole is the khabar of inna. (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is (ما لَكُمْ مِنْ وَلايَتِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ). Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read «من ولايتهم» [Translator's note: i.e. with kasra, wilāyatihim; the vowelling is not shown in the source]. One says: walīy (a patron) with evident walāya, and wālin (a ruler) with evident wilāya. Abū Jaʿfar said: The fatḥa here is clearer and better, because it means "help/support". Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: The kasra is permissible because it is comprehensive, so it became like ṣināʿa (craft) and khiyāṭa (tailoring). He said: (فَعَلَيْكُمُ النَّصْرُ) may also be read in the accusative as an ighrāʾ (incitement) [Translator's note: i.e. al-naṣra, "upon you is [to give] help!"].

nahhas-irab:73-73.t: Al-Kisāʾī said: The accusative is permissible in His words (تَكُنْ فِتْنَةٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَفَسادٌ كَبِيرٌ) [Translator's note: i.e. fitnatan … wa-fasādan kabīran, with kāna taken as incomplete and an implied ism].

nahhas-irab:74-74.t: (حَقًّا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) [Translator's note: i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)].

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: (وَأُولُوا الْأَرْحامِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); its singular is «ذو», and raḥim (womb, kinship) is feminine. (بَعْضُهُمْ): a mubtadaʾ; (أَوْلى بِبَعْضٍ): the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of the first. Concerning His words (فِي كِتابِ اللَّهِ), Majestic and Mighty is He [Translator's note: the source has «جلّ وعزّل.», an evident typo], there are several views. Among them: that this verse shows that no one inherits except one who has a mention in the Book of Allah, unless the Muslims agree by consensus on something or it is authentically established from the Messenger ﷺ. It is also said that the meaning of (فِي كِتابِ اللَّهِ) is "in the Preserved Tablet". It is also said that (فِي كِتابِ اللَّهِ) means "in the ruling of Allah", as the Prophet ﷺ said: «لأقضينّ بينكما بكتاب الله» ("I will surely judge between you two by the Book of Allah"), Majestic and Mighty is He; and he judged with flogging and a year's banishment, and stoning for her if she was muḥṣana (married), while stoning is not in the Qur'an. So it was said: the meaning of «بكتاب الله», Majestic and Mighty is He, is "by the ruling of Allah". It was also said: since He, Majestic and Mighty, said (وَما آتاكُمُ الرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَما نَهاكُمْ عَنْهُ فَانْتَهُوا) [al-Ḥashr: 7], accepting from the Prophet ﷺ is by the Book of Allah, Majestic and Mighty. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ): the ism of «إنّ» and its khabar.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: يَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْأَنْفالِ: if you lighten the hamza you cast its vowel onto the sīn and drop it. Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, may Allah be pleased with him, read يسئلونك الأنفال; it would be by way of explanation, and يسألونك is made transitive to two objects. قُلِ الْأَنْفالُ لِلَّهِ is mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). وَالرَّسُولِ is conjoined. فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَصْلِحُوا ذاتَ بَيْنِكُمْ: i.e. be united upon the command of Allah, Mighty and Exalted; and in the supplication: «اللهمّ أصلح ذات البين» ("O Allah, set right [the state] between [us]"), i.e. the condition by which unity comes about. وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ: concerning the spoils and other matters.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ما» is restrictive (kāffa); the accusative is permissible by analogy, but Sībawayh disallowed it.
الَّذِينَ إِذا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. Sībawayh related وجل يوجل, ياجل, ييجل and ييجل [i.e. yaujal, yājal, yayjal, yījal]. Abū Zayd said: I asked al-Khalīl about those who said رأيت الزّيدان [i.e. with alif in the accusative dual], and he said: this is according to the dialect of those who say ياجل.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ is a badal (substitute) of the first «الذين».

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ is mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). حَقًّا is a maṣdar (verbal noun). لَهُمْ دَرَجاتٌ is a mubtadaʾ [with fronted khabar], i.e. lofty ranks in Paradise in proportion to their deeds. وَمَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ is conjoined.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
كَما أَخْرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَيْتِكَ بِالْحَقِّ is among the difficult [passages], and the philologists have six views on it. Saʿīd ibn Masʿada said: "those are the believers truly, just as your Lord brought you out of your house with the truth". He said: and one of the scholars said: "just as your Lord brought you out of your house with the truth, so fear Allah and set right [what is] between you". Al-Kisāʾī said: i.e. their disputing with him now is just as your Lord brought you out of your house with the truth. Abū ʿUbayda said:
it is an oath, i.e. "by the One who brought you out of your house". Abū Isḥāq said: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. the spoils are confirmed for you, just as your Lord brought you out of your house with the truth while they were averse; likewise We grant spoils to whom you see fit. These are five views, and this view of Abū Isḥāq is the meaning of the view of al-Farrāʾ, because al-Farrāʾ said: carry on with your command regarding the spoils and grant extra shares to whom you will, even if they are averse, just as your Lord brought you out of your house with the truth. The sixth view, one of the best of them: Allah, Mighty and Exalted, said إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ إِذا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ up to لَهُمْ ... مَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ; so the meaning is: this promise to the believers is true, just as your Lord brought you out of your house with the truth that was binding upon Him, and so He fulfilled your promise and gave you victory over your enemy and kept faith with you, for He, Mighty and Exalted, said: وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ اللَّهُ إِحْدَى الطَّائِفَتَيْنِ أَنَّها لَكُمْ وَتَوَدُّونَ [al-Anfāl: 7]; so just as He fulfilled this promise in this world, so too [He will fulfil] what He promised you in the Hereafter.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: The meaning of يُجادِلُونَكَ is "some of them dispute with you"; the pronoun refers back to "some" because they have been mentioned within the whole. The meaning of "after it had become clear" is that since everything the Prophet ﷺ told them came to pass, it became binding on them to accept from him everything he said, and the truth had become clear to them.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t:
إِحْدَى الطَّائِفَتَيْنِ is the second object. أَنَّها لَكُمْ is a badal (substitute). وَتَوَدُّونَ أَنَّ غَيْرَ ذاتِ الشَّوْكَةِ تَكُونُ لَكُمْ: Abū ʿUbayda said: i.e. other than the one possessing an edge. Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. you wished to prevail over the party that had no weapons with it and in which there was no fighting. One says فلان شاكٍ في السلاح, شائك and شاكّ ("bristling with weapons"), from الشّكّة ("arms"), as he said: [al-Munsariḥ] 166-
إمّا تري شكّتي رميح أبي ... سعد فقد أحمل السّلاح معا
(If you see that my arms are [only] the little spear of Abū Saʿd — well, I have borne full weapons together.)

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: لِيُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ: i.e. to make His promise come true. وَيُبْطِلَ الْباطِلَ: i.e. the scheming of the disbelievers.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ: because of your small number; i.e. "remember". فَاسْتَجابَ لَكُمْ أَنِّي is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "that I…" [lit. "with that I"]. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read (إنّي), in the sense of "He said: I…". And it is related from ʿĀṣim أَنِّي مُمِدُّكُمْ بِأَلْفٍ مِنَ الْمَلائِكَةِ [i.e. بِأُلُفٍ], as you say فلس and أفلس. [Translator's note: the variant form is not marked in the source.] مُرْدِفِينَ is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba and Nāfiʿ [i.e. مُرْدَفِين]; Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza read مُرْدِفِينَ with kasra on the dāl. Sībawayh said: some read مُرَدِّفِينَ with fatḥa on the rāʾ and a doubled dāl, some مُرِدِّفين with kasra on the rāʾ, and some مُرُدِّفين with ḍamma on the rāʾ, the dāl having kasra in all three readings. «مردَفين» with fatḥa on the dāl has two construals: it may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «كم» in ممدكم, i.e. the believers were reinforced by them, and this is the view of Mujāhid; Mujāhid said: i.e. reinforced. Abū Jaʿfar said: and «مردفين» may be in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «الألف». As for «مردِفين» with kasra on the dāl, Abū ʿAmr said of it: i.e. some of them followed others. Abū ʿUbayd rebutted Abū ʿAmr on this view and rejected the kasra on the dāl, arguing that the meaning of أردف فلان فلانا is "he put him behind him [on a mount]". He said: we do not know this in the description of the angels on the day of Badr. And he rejected أردف being in the sense of ردف, because of the saying of Allah, Mighty and Exalted: تَتْبَعُهَا الرَّادِفَةُ [al-Nāziʿāt: 7], where He did not say المردفة. Abū Jaʿfar said: this rebuttal does not bind Abū ʿAmr, and his words are not to be interpreted as Abū ʿUbayd interpreted them; rather the meaning of مردِفين is that some of them came before others. One says:
ردفته and أردفته in the sense of تبعته and أتبعته ("I followed him"). Had it been as Abū ʿUbayd said, the meaning of مردَفين with fatḥa on the dāl would be "made to ride behind you"; but the meaning of مردِفين is only "on your tracks", i.e. some of them followed others. This is stronger than the view of whoever said "by whom the Muslims are reinforced", because the apparent sense of the Qurʾān is contrary to it. The reading مردِفين is preferable, because the exegetes interpret according to this reading: i.e. some of them followed others. As for مرَدِّفين, its construal according to Sībawayh is
مرتدفين; then the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl and its vowel cast onto the rāʾ so that two unvowelled letters would not meet. Whoever said
مرِدِّفين gave the rāʾ kasra because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters, and whoever said مرُدِّفين with ḍamma on the rāʾ [did so because] there is a ḍamma before it, as you say: ردُّ يا هذا.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: وَما جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشْرى: two objects. بُشْرى is not declined because it contains the alif of the feminine. وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ: the lām of purpose (lām kay), and the verb is omitted because [the context] indicates it. وَمَا النَّصْرُ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is إِلَّا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ. إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ: the noun of «إنّ» and its khabar.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: إِذْ يُغَشِّيكُمُ النُّعاسَ: two objects; it is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries [sic], and it is good because after it comes وَيُنَزِّلُ عَلَيْكُمْ. [Translator's note: in the standard transmission the reading of the people of Medina is يُغْشِيكُم and Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read يَغْشاكُمُ النُّعاسُ; the attribution is translated as printed.] أَمَنَةً is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) and a maṣdar (verbal noun); one says أمنة, أمنا and أمانا. لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ is accusative by the lām of purpose (lām kay), because it substitutes for «أن», or by an implied «أن». وَيُذْهِبَ عَنْكُمْ رِجْزَ الشَّيْطانِ is conjoined. وَلِيَرْبِطَ عَلى قُلُوبِكُمْ: conjunction of a clause to a clause, or of a single item, and the lām is repeated. وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ: by the water that Allah, Mighty and Exalted, sent down upon the sand on the day of Badr so that the feet of the Muslims became firm; and «به» may refer to the strengthening (ribāṭ).

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: إِذْ يُوحِي رَبُّكَ: i.e. He makes [feet] firm by it at that time; and it may be "remember". إِذْ يُوحِي رَبُّكَ إِلَى الْمَلائِكَةِ أَنِّي is in the position of the accusative, the meaning being "that I…" [lit. "with that I"]. مَعَكُمْ is an adverb (ẓarf); whoever makes the ʿayn unvowelled takes it in his view as a particle. Al-Akhfash said: فاضربوا فوق الأعناق means "strike the necks"; according to Muḥammad ibn Yazīd this is a mistake, because فوق conveys a meaning and so cannot be redundant; rather the meaning is that they were permitted to strike the faces and what is near them. وَاضْرِبُوا مِنْهُمْ كُلَّ بَنانٍ: Abū Isḥāq said: the singular of البنان is بنانة, and here it means the fingers and other limbs. The derivation of البنان is from their saying أبنّ بالمكان when one stays in a place; so with the banān one does what serves for staying and living.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t:
[ذل]ِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ شَاقُّوا اللَّهَ [Translator's note: the opening of this entry is truncated in the source.]
(ذلك) is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), or as khabar (predicate); the implied structure is "that is the matter" or "the matter is that". مَنْ يُشاقِقِ اللَّهَ
is jussive by the condition; وَمَنْ يُشَاقِّ اللَّهَ is also permissible, as Jarīr said: [al-Wāfir] 167-
فغضّ الطّرف إنّك من نمير ... فلا كعبا بلغت ولا كلابا
(So lower your gaze, for you are of Numayr; you have reached neither Kaʿb nor Kilāb.)
And «ومن يشاقَّ الله» is permissible, and the implied structure is [فإنّ اللهَ شَ]دِيدُ الْعِقابِ له, and «له» is omitted. [Translator's note: the text here is truncated in the source; the restored words in square brackets follow the ayah.]

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
ذلِكُمْ فَذُوقُوهُ: as was stated for the first. وَأَنَّ is in the position of the nominative by its being conjoined to «ذلكم». Al-Farrāʾ said: it may be in the position of the accusative in the sense of «وبأنّ للكافرين». He said:
and it is possible to imply "and know that". Abū Isḥāq said: if implying "and know" were permissible, زيد منطلق وعمرا جالسا would be permissible; indeed, in the mubtadaʾ-construction زيدا منطلقا would be permissible, because the one informing is making known — and none of the grammarians says this.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: إِذا لَقِيتُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا زَحْفاً: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: وَمَنْ يُوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ دُبُرَهُ is a condition. إِلَّا مُتَحَرِّفاً لِقِتالٍ أَوْ مُتَحَيِّزاً إِلى فِئَةٍ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). فَقَدْ باءَ بِغَضَبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ is the requital. وَمَأْواهُ جَهَنَّمُ is mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: And likewise وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ on the reading of whoever lightened «لكن» [i.e. ولكنِ اللهُ قتلهم]. The meaning of فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ is: you did not kill them by your own planning, but Allah killed them through victory. The like of this is that if two men were fighting, each with a sword, and a man came and took the sword of one of them, and the other killed him, it could be said: "No one killed that man but the one who took his sword." وَما رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ رَمى is like it; and it is possible that the meaning is: "you did not cast terror into their hearts when you threw the pebbles".

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: ذلِكُمْ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مُوهِنُ كَيْدِ الْكافِرِينَ is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries and Abū ʿAmr [i.e. مُوَهِّنٌ كَيْدَ]; the reading of the people of Kufa is مُوهِنُ كَيْدِ الْكافِرِينَ [i.e. مُوهِنٌ كَيْدَ]. In the doubling there is the sense of intensity. It is related from al-Ḥasan مُوهِنُ كَيْدِ الْكافِرِينَ with annexation and lightening. [Translator's note: the source places the doubled form with the Kufans' reading and does not mark the vowels; in the standard transmission Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read مُوَهِّنٌ, and Ḥafṣ مُوهِنُ كَيْدِ.] The meaning is that Allah, Mighty and Exalted, casts terror into their hearts until they are scattered or their gathering is dispersed.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: إِنْ تَسْتَفْتِحُوا فَقَدْ جاءَكُمُ الْفَتْحُ: there are three views on its meaning. It may be an address to the disbelievers, because they said: "O Allah, give victory to whichever of the two parties is dearer to You". وَإِنْ تَنْتَهُوا: i.e. from disbelief. وَإِنْ تَعُودُوا: to this saying; نَعُدْ: to giving victory to the believers. It was said: إن تستفتحوا is an address to the believers, i.e. if you seek victory, victory has come to you; and likewise «وإن تنتهوا», i.e. if you desist from the like of what you did in taking spoils and captives before permission, فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ; and if you return to the like of that, We will return to rebuking you, as He, Mighty and Exalted, said: لَوْلا كِتابٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ سَبَقَ لَمَسَّكُمْ فِيما أَخَذْتُمْ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ [al-Anfāl: 68]. The third view is that إن تستفتحوا فقد جاءكم الفتح is [addressed] to the believers and what follows it to the disbelievers. وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: i.e. with the obedient believers. (أنّ) has fatḥa in the sense of "and because Allah…"; the implied structure is "because of its great number, and because Allah…", and «أنّ» is in the position of the accusative on this view. It was also said: it is conjoined to «وأن الله موهّن». The kasra is on resumption.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: Mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) [i.e. وَأَنْتُمْ تَسْمَعُونَ]; the meaning is "while you hear the arguments and proofs that are recited to you".

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: وَلا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as an adverb [sic], and [it is] the khabar of كان. سَمِعْنا may be in the sense of "we accepted", as is said: سمع الله لمن حمده ("Allah hears/accepts the one who praises Him"); it may be from hearing with the ear; and it may be in the sense of وهم لا يشعرون — they do not reflect on what they heard nor think about it, so they are in the position of one who has not heard. [Translator's note: «على الظرف» is as printed.]

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: إِنَّ شَرَّ الدَّوَابِّ: the original is أشرّ; the hamza was dropped because of frequent use; and likewise «خير», whose original is أخير. الصُّمُّ الْبُكْمُ الَّذِينَ لا يَعْقِلُونَ: the khabar of «إنّ» and a naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: وَلَوْ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ فِيهِمْ خَيْراً لَأَسْمَعَهُمْ: i.e. He would have made them hear the answer to everything they ask about. This is indicated by [His saying]: and had He made them hear, لَتَوَلَّوْا وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ — so He informed about them concerning the unseen.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
إِذا دَعاكُمْ لِما يُحْيِيكُمْ: the ḍamma was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness, and assimilation is not permissible.
وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِ: (أنّ) is in the position of the accusative by اعلموا. وَأَنَّهُ إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ is conjoined. Al-Farrāʾ said: had it been resumptive, with «وإنّه» given kasra, it would have been correct.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and we have mentioned لا تُصِيبَنَّ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْكُمْ خَاصَّةً.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: إِذْ أَنْتُمْ قَلِيلٌ is mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). مُسْتَضْعَفُونَ is a naʿt (adjective), and likewise تَخافُونَ. أَنْ يَتَخَطَّفَكُمُ النَّاسُ is in the position of the accusative.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: لا تَخُونُوا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ: by embezzling the spoils. He attributed it to Allah, Mighty and Exalted, because He commanded its division, and to the Messenger ﷺ because he is the one who conveys from Allah, Mighty and Exalted, and the one in charge of it. وَتَخُونُوا is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the first; and it may be accusative as an answer, as one says: لا تأكل السمك وتشرب اللّبن ("do not eat fish and [at the same time] drink milk").

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: إِنْ تَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ فُرْقاناً: i.e. He will make between you and the disbelievers a distinction, by giving you victory and honour, and abandoning and humiliating them.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: i.e. "and remember this". لِيُثْبِتُوكَ is accusative by the lām of purpose (lām kay); it was said its meaning is "to confine you", and one of the philologists related أثبته when he wounded him so that he could not move. أَوْ يَقْتُلُوكَ أَوْ يُخْرِجُوكَ is conjoined. وَيَمْكُرُونَ is resumptive. وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْماكِرِينَ is mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The meaning is that the scheming of Allah, Mighty and Exalted, is only that He brings upon them the punishment they deserve from where they do not perceive; so He is the best of schemers.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: وَإِذْ قالُوا اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كانَ هذا هُوَ الْحَقَّ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ: [الحقّ] is the khabar of كان. هُوَ, according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, is a separator (fāṣila). Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Abū Isḥāq explain the meaning of fāṣila; he said: because it was brought only so that it be known that the khabar is definite or close to definite, that الْحَقَّ is not a naʿt (adjective), and that كانَ is not in the sense of «وقع» ("occurred"). Al-Akhfash said: (هو) is a redundant connective (ṣila zāʾida), like the redundancy of «ما»; and the Kufans said: (هو) is a support (ʿimād). Al-Akhfash said: Banū Tamīm put it in the nominative, saying: إن كان هذا هو الحقُّ من عندك. Abū Jaʿfar said: (هو) is then a mubtadaʾ and «الحقّ» its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of كان.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: We have mentioned وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ with full explanation.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
Al-Akhfash said: in وَما لَهُمْ أَلَّا يُعَذِّبَهُمُ اللَّهُ, «أن» is redundant (zāʾida).
Abū Jaʿfar said: had it been as he said, يعذّبهم would be nominative. (أن) is in the position of the accusative, and the meaning is "what prevents them from being punished?"; «أن» entered for this meaning. وَهُمْ يَصُدُّونَ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ is mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and likewise إِنْ أَوْلِياؤُهُ إِلَّا الْمُتَّقُونَ. وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ — and it is incumbent on them to know. It was said: they do not know that they will be punished in the Hereafter, though it is possible that He will forgive them; and it was said: they do not know that the God-fearing are His allies.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t:
وَما كانَ صَلاتُهُمْ is the noun of كان; إِلَّا مُكاءً is the khabar (predicate). Abū Ḥātim said: Hārūn said: it reached me that al-Aʿmash read وَما كانَ صَلاتُهُمْ عِنْدَ الْبَيْتِ إِلَّا مُكاءً وَتَصْدِيَةً [i.e. صلاتَهم … إلا مكاءٌ وتصديةٌ]. Abū Jaʿfar said: Sībawayh permitted the like of this as anomalous and far-fetched, because it makes the noun of كان indefinite and its khabar definite. Sībawayh recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 168-
أسكران كان ابن المراغة إذ هجا ... تميما ببطن الشّام أم متساكر
(Was Ibn al-Marāgha drunk when he lampooned Tamīm in the heart of Syria, or feigning drunkenness?)
And he recited: [al-Wāfir] 169-
فإنّك لا تبالي بعد حول ... أظبي كان أمّك أم حمار
(For after a year you will not care whether your mother was a gazelle or a donkey.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: clearer than this — even though he has qualified the indefinite — is his saying: [al-Wāfir] 170-
ولا يك موقف منك الوداعا
(And let not a standing from you be the farewell.)
And likewise: [al-Wāfir] 171-
يكون مزاجها عسل وماء
(Its mixture is honey and water.)
— even though ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān said: the implied structure is "as a mixture for it". وتصدية is from صدّ يصدّ when one shouts; a yāʾ was substituted for one of the two dāls.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: لِيَمِيزَ is accusative by the lām of purpose (lām kay), and لِيُمَيِّزَ is for intensity. وَيَجْعَلَ and فَيَرْكُمَهُ are conjoined.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: إِنْ يَنْتَهُوا يُغْفَرْ لَهُمْ is condition and requital, and likewise وَإِنْ يَعُودُوا فَقَدْ مَضَتْ سُنَّتُ الْأَوَّلِينَ, i.e. the practice regarding the earlier peoples has gone before, in the punishment of those who persist in disobedience to Allah, Mighty and Exalted.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: حَتَّى لا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ: [فتنة] is the noun of تكون, and it [تكون] is in the sense of "occur"; and likewise وَيَكُونَ الدِّينُ كُلُّهُ لِلَّهِ.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: نِعْمَ الْمَوْلى: nominative by نعم, because it is a verb. Abū ʿUmar al-Jarmī said: the proof that it is a verb is the Arabs' saying نعمت, retaining the tāʾ. And likewise وَنِعْمَ النَّصِيرُ.

nahhas-irab:41-42.t:
وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّما غَنِمْتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ: «ما» is in the sense of «الذي», and the hāʾ [the resumptive pronoun] is omitted. The fāʾ entered because there is a sense of requital in the speech. The second «أنّ» is an emphasis (tawkīd) of the first, and kasra on it is permissible. خُمُسَهُ is the noun of إنّ. يَوْمَ الْفُرْقانِ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعانِ are two adverbs, and likewise إِذْ أَنْتُمْ بِالْعُدْوَةِ الدُّنْيا. The plural is عُدًى; whoever says عِدوة says عِدًى, like لحية and لحًى. One says «القصيا», and the original has wāw [i.e. القصوى].
وَالرَّكْبُ is a mubtadaʾ (subject). It was said that by it is meant the camels that carried their goods, which were in a place where they were safe for them, as a grace from Allah, Mighty and Exalted; so He reminded them of His favours to them. And it was said: it means the caravan of Quraysh.
أَسْفَلَ مِنْكُمْ is an adverb in the position of the khabar (predicate), i.e. "in a place lower than you". Al-Akhfash, al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted والركب أسفلُ منكم [in the nominative], i.e. "more low-lying than you". الركب is the plural of راكب, and the Arabs do not say ركب except for a group riding camels. Ibn al-Sikkīt and most of the philologists related that راكب and ركب are said only of those on camels specifically; one does not say
راكب of one who is on a horse or other [animal]. وَلَوْ تَواعَدْتُمْ لَاخْتَلَفْتُمْ فِي الْمِيعادِ: i.e. agreement would not have come about, but Allah, Mighty and Exalted, brought it about for you. لِيَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ أَمْراً كانَ مَفْعُولًا: of giving victory to the believers. لِيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ: the lām of purpose (lām kay); the implied structure is "but He gathered you there to decree a matter". In ليهلك this lām is repeated on the lām in ليقضي, and مَنْ is in the position of the nominative. وَيَحْيى is in the position of the accusative. مَنْ حَيَّ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr and Ḥamza, and it is the choice of Sībawayh and Abū ʿUbayd. As for Abū ʿUbayd's argument, it is that in the written text (al-sawād) it is with a single yāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar said:
this argument is not binding, because the like of this omission occurs in the written text; rather, the consensus of the skilled grammarians in this is that when two letters of the same form come together, assimilation is preferable, as one says جفّ. Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim read من حيي عن بيّنة, and the argument for them is that assimilation is not permissible in the imperfect, so they made the past follow the imperfect. Al-Farrāʾ permitted assimilation in the imperfect, and that يحيّى be assimilated; according to all the Basrans this is a great mistake, and the like of it is permissible neither in poetry nor in speech. The reason for disallowing it is that when you say يحيى the second yāʾ is unvowelled, so two vowelled letters have not come together so as to be assimilated. [Compare:] the preferred form is لم يجفف, though لم يجفَّ and لم يجفِّ are permissible, so assimilation is permissible [there]; but in يحيى it is not permissible. Moreover the yāʾ is dropped in the jussive, so this differs from يجفّ. Nor is assimilation permissible in أَلَيْسَ ذلِكَ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتى [al-Qiyāma: 40], because the vowel is incidental.

nahhas-irab:43-44.t: إِذْ يُرِيكَهُمُ اللَّهُ is an adverb, and likewise وَإِذْ يُرِيكُمُوهُمْ. It came attached because you began with the nearer [pronoun]; Yūnus permitted يريكمهم.

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: وَلا تَنازَعُوا is a prohibition. فَتَفْشَلُوا is accusative because it is the answer to the prohibition. Sībawayh does not permit dropping the fāʾ and using the jussive; al-Kisāʾī permitted it.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: وَلا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ بَطَراً: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). The meaning of baṭar in the language is strengthening oneself, by the favours of Allah, Mighty and Exalted — the well-being with which Allah, Mighty and Exalted, has clothed one — in acts of disobedience.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: وَإِنِّي جارٌ لَكُمْ: جار is pluralised أجوار and جيران, and for a small number جيرة. إِنِّي أَخافُ اللَّهَ: it was said: he feared that an affliction would descend upon him.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: إِذْ يَقُولُ الْمُنافِقُونَ وَالَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ: it was said that the hypocrites are those who displayed faith and concealed disbelief, and those in whose hearts is a disease are the doubters, who are below the hypocrites. And it was said: they are one and the same, and this is preferable. Do you not see His saying, Mighty and Exalted: الَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ [al-Baqara: 3], then He, Mighty and Exalted, said: وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكَ [al-Baqara: 4], and both refer to one [group]; and likewise إِنَّ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَالْمُسْلِماتِ وَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ [al-Aḥzāb: 35].

nahhas-irab:50-50.t:
This may be at death, and it may be on the Day of Resurrection when they take them to the Fire. The apodosis of «لو» is omitted, its implied form being "you would have seen a tremendous matter". Saʿīd al-Akhfash recited: [al-Khafīf] 172-
إن يكن طبّك الدّلال فلو في ... سالف الدّهر والسّنين الخوالي
(If your habit is coquetry — [well,] had it been in bygone times and the years gone by…)
Al-Aʿraj read تتوفّى, treating the group as feminine. يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is "and they say: وَذُوقُوا عَذابَ الْحَرِيقِ".

nahhas-irab:51-51.t:
ذلِكَ is in the position of the nominative, i.e. "the matter is that". بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ is genitive by the bāʾ [the source prints: الياء].
وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلَّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to (ما); and if you wish you may make it accusative in the sense of «وبأنّ» with the bāʾ dropped, [or] in the sense of "and that is that Allah…"; and it may be in the position of the nominative, conjoined to ذلك.

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ: i.e. the custom in punishing them at the taking of the souls and in the graves is like the custom with the people of Pharaoh. وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ: of the disbelievers. After this there is again كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ, and this is not a repetition, because the first concerns the custom in punishment and the second the custom in changing [favour].

nahhas-irab:55-56.t: إِنَّ شَرَّ الدَّوَابِّ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: the noun of «إنّ» and its khabar (predicate). It is specific, and He, Mighty and Exalted, has made it clear by His saying: الَّذِينَ عاهَدْتَ مِنْهُمْ ثُمَّ يَنْقُضُونَ عَهْدَهُمْ فِي كُلِّ مَرَّةٍ وَهُمْ لا يَتَّقُونَ.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t:
فَإِمَّا تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ is a condition; the nūn entered for emphasis, and that became fitting in a statement when (ما) entered — this is the view of the Basrans. The Kufans said: the heavy and the light nūn enter with إمّا in requital to distinguish between requital and choice. فَشَرِّدْ بِهِمْ مَنْ خَلْفَهُمْ: al-Kisāʾī said: (من) is in the sense of «الذي».
Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is: do to them a deed of killing by which you scatter those behind them. لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ: i.e. they will remember your threat to them.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: وَإِمَّا تَخافَنَّ مِنْ قَوْمٍ خِيانَةً فَانْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَلى سَواءٍ: al-Kisāʾī said: al-sawāʾ is justice. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is said that its meaning is "do to them as they do, equally". He said: and it is said that the meaning of فَانْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَلى سَواءٍ is "openly, not secretly". Abū Jaʿfar said: this is among the inimitable things that have come in the Qurʾān, the like of which is not found in speech, in its brevity and the abundance of its meanings. The meaning is: if you fear treachery from a people between whom and you there is a covenant, then throw the covenant back to them, i.e. say: "I have thrown back your covenant to you, and I am going to fight you", so that they know that and are equal with you in knowledge; and do not fight them while there is a covenant between you and them and they are relying on you, for that would be treachery. Then He made this clear by His saying: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْخائِنِينَ.

nahhas-irab:59-59.t:
ولا تحسبن الذين كفروا سبقوا: the noun of تحسبنّ and its khabar (predicate) [i.e. its two objects]. Ḥamza read وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَبَقُوا, and a group of grammarians, among them Abū Ḥātim, claimed that this is a solecism, that reading with it is not lawful, and that it should not be heard from anyone who knows i'rab or has been taught it. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a severe bias; and Abū Ḥātim said more than this. He said: because no object came for يحسبنّ, while it needs two objects. Abū Jaʿfar said: the reading is permissible, and the meaning would be "and let those behind them not think that those who disbelieve have outstripped [them]", so the pronoun refers back to what preceded; but the reading with the tāʾ is clearer. Al-Farrāʾ said:
and in the text (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ولا يحسب الذين كفروا أنهم سبقوا أنهم لا يعجزون. And it is related ولا تحسبَ الذين with fatḥa on the bāʾ, and this is by intending the light nūn, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 173-
وسبّح على حين العشيّات والضّحى ... ولا تحمد المثرين والله فاحمدا
(Glorify [Allah] in the evenings and the forenoon, and do not praise the wealthy — praise Allah.)
And if you wish you may give the dāl kasra. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĀmir read إِنَّهُمْ لا يُعْجِزُونَ with fatḥa on the hamza [i.e. أنّهم], and Abū Ḥātim and Abū ʿUbayd considered this reading far-fetched. Abū ʿUbayd said: it is only permissible on the basis that the meaning is "and do not think that those who disbelieve, that they cannot frustrate". Abū Jaʿfar said: what Abū ʿUbayd mentioned is not permissible according to the Basran grammarians: حسبت زيدا أنه خارج is not permissible except with kasra on إنّ; it is impermissible only because it is in the position of the mubtadaʾ, as you say: حسبت زيدا أبوه خارج; had you used fatḥa, the meaning would become "I thought Zayd [to be] his going out", and this is absurd. There is also in it the remoteness that what he said has no construal by which a meaning would be sound unless you make «إلّا» [sic] redundant; and there is no ground for attributing an omission in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Exalted, by way of elaboration without a proof that must be accepted. [Translator's note: «إلّا» is as printed; «لا» is presumably meant.] The reading is good on the basis that the meaning is "because they cannot frustrate". Al-Farrāʾ claimed that Ḥamza's reading is permissible by implying «أن», the meaning being "and let not those who disbelieve think that they have outstripped". Abū Jaʿfar said: implying «أن» is not permissible except with a compensation, and whoever implies it has implied part of a noun. Al-Farrāʾ likened this to their saying عسى يقوم زيد, but it does not resemble it, because if «أن» were implied here it would make يقوم accusative. We have mentioned that whoever read لا يُعْجِزُونَ with kasra on the nūn [i.e. يُعْجِزُونِ] has committed a solecism.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: وَأَعِدُّوا لَهُمْ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ: everything you prepare for your friend of good, or for your enemy of evil, is included in your preparation (ʿudda). Al-Ḥasan read (تُرْهِبُونَ بِهِ عَدُوَّ اللَّهِ) for intensity [i.e. تُرَهِّبون], and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read عَدُوًّا لِلَّهِ. وَآخَرِينَ مِنْ دُونِهِمْ is conjoined to عدوّ, and it may be conjoined to وأعدّوا لهم by an implied verb.

nahhas-irab:61-61.t: وَإِنْ جَنَحُوا لِلسَّلْمِ فَاجْنَحْ لَها: [the feminine pronoun] because السلم is feminine; and the feminine may be for "the deed" (al-faʿla). Abū Ḥātim related فَاجْنَحْ لها [i.e. فاجنُح, with ḍamma on the nūn]. [Translator's note: the variant vocalisation is not marked in the source.]

nahhas-irab:64-64.t:
يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ حَسْبُكَ اللَّهُ is mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. "Allah suffices you"; one says أحسبه when one suffices him. وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to the kāf in interpretation, i.e. "Allah suffices you and suffices whoever follows you", as he said: [al-Ṭawīl] 174-
إذا كانت الهيجاء وانشقّت العصا ... فحسبك والضّحّاك سيف مهنّد
(When battle comes and the staff is split [i.e. unity is broken], an Indian sword suffices you and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.)
وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ may also be in the position of the nominative, and on this the grammarians have three views. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: it is conjoined to the name of Allah, Mighty and Exalted, i.e. "Allah suffices you, and whoever follows you"; he said: and like it is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Allah and the sons of Qayla will suffice me against him." The second view is that the implied structure is "and whoever follows you of the believers [is] likewise", as a mubtadaʾ with [its] khabar [omitted], as al-Farazdaq said: [al-Ṭawīl] 175-
وعضّ زمان يا ابن مروان لم يدع ... من المال إلّا مسحتا أو مجلّف
(And the bite of a time, O son of Marwān, that has left of wealth nothing but what is wiped out or barely remaining.)
The third view — the best of them — is that it is by an implied element, in the sense of "and whoever follows you of the believers suffices you"; and the ḥadīth is likewise by an implied element: "and whoever suffices". [The first view is weak] because it is soundly established from the Prophet ﷺ that he forbade saying "What Allah wills and you will"; and as for the second view, the poet is under constraint in it, since the poem rhymes in the nominative, even if there are other [explanations] of it. [Translator's note: the bracketed words supply what the source leaves implicit.]

nahhas-irab:65-65.t: إِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صابِرُونَ: [عشرون] is the noun of «يكن». If someone asks: why is the first letter of عشرين given kasra, while the first of ثلاثين and what follows up to ثمانين is given fatḥa, except ستّين? The answer according to Sībawayh is that عشرين relates to عشرة as اثنين relates to واحد, so the first of عشرين was given kasra as اثنان is; and the proof of this is their saying ستّون and تسعون just as ستّة and تسعة are said.

nahhas-irab:66-66.t: Abū Jaʿfar read وعلم أنّ فيكم ضعفاء, as one says كريم and كرماء. The reading of the people of Medina and Abū ʿAmr is ضعفا [i.e. ضُعْفًا], and it is the choice of Abū Ḥātim and Abū ʿUbayd. Abū ʿUbayd said: because of the large number who read it, and because it is the reading of the Prophet ﷺ and of those who followed him in it. As for this statement — though it is known of Abū ʿUbayd, may Allah have mercy on him, that he intended nothing but good — "and those who followed him" is said only of someone whom it is permissible to differ from; and the chain of the ḥadīth is not strong. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ said: al-ḍuʿf is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz and al-ḍaʿf is the dialect of Tamīm; as for distinguishing between them, it is not sound — I mean in meaning.

nahhas-irab:67-67.t: أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ أَسْرى: and تكون [is permissible], treating the group as feminine. [The plural is] أسرى, أُسارى and أَسارى. تُرِيدُونَ عَرَضَ الدُّنْيا: i.e. the spoils and the ransom. وَاللَّهُ يُرِيدُ الْآخِرَةَ: i.e. He wants for you the reward of the Hereafter, because it is better for you.

nahhas-irab:68-68.t:
There are five answers concerning it. Among the best of them is that the meaning is: "were it not for a Book from Allah that came down — the Qurʾān — so that you believed in it and thus deserved pardon and forgiveness, He would have punished you." And it was said: the meaning is: "were it not for a Book from Allah that came down — the Qurʾān — so that you believed in it and thus deserved pardon and forgiveness, He would have punished you." And it was said: the meaning is: "were it not that Allah, Mighty and Exalted, had written that He would make spoils lawful for you, He would have punished you." The fifth answer is that the meaning is: "were it not that Allah, Mighty and Exalted, had written that He would forgive the people of Badr their past and future sins, He would have punished you." [Translator's note: the source repeats the first answer verbatim and lists only four distinct answers.] The meaning of لَوْلا in the language is the non-occurrence of something because of the occurrence of something. كِتابٌ is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and سَبَقَ is in the position of a naʿt (adjective) of it; it cannot be the khabar, because it is not permissible to supply a khabar for what is made nominative as mubtadaʾ after لولا. This is the view of Sībawayh. The implied structure is "were it not for a Book from Allah that preceded, overtaking you". لَمَسَّكُمْ: its original is faʿila, then it was assimilated; the overt form is permissible, as he said: [al-Basīṭ] 176-
مهلا أعاذل قد جرّبت من خلقي ... أنّى أجود لأقوام وإن ضننوا
(Gently, O reproaching woman! You have tried my nature: I am generous to people even if they are stingy.)
فِيما أَخَذْتُمْ: the dhāl was assimilated into the tāʾ because the voiceless (mahmūs) letter is lighter; the overt form is permissible here.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t: فَكُلُوا مِمَّا غَنِمْتُمْ: in the fāʾ there is the sense of condition and requital. And Sībawayh said: "Words are noun, verb and particle." [Translator's note: this quotation from the opening of Sībawayh's Kitāb, introduced with a fāʾ, is presumably cited as a parallel for a fāʾ introducing what follows an implied premise.] The implied structure in the ayah is: "I have made the ransom lawful for you, so eat of what you have taken as spoils". حَلالًا طَيِّباً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:70-70.t: يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ قُلْ لِمَنْ فِي أَيْدِيكُمْ مِنَ الْأَسْرى: He addressed the Prophet ﷺ, then said لِمَنْ فِي أَيْدِيكُمْ. There are three answers on this. The meaning may be: "O Prophet, tell them: say to the captives who are in your hands". It may be that the address to him ﷺ is an address to his community, as He, Mighty and Exalted, said: يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ [al-Ṭalāq: 1]. And it may be by a shift of address, [as] in إِذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ. As for its being for veneration [i.e. the plural of majesty], that is far-fetched. إِنْ يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ خَيْراً is a condition; the mīm has kasra because of the meeting of two unvowelled letters; and the apodosis is يُؤْتِكُمْ, so the yāʾ was dropped from it.

nahhas-irab:71-71.t: وَإِنْ يُرِيدُوا خِيانَتَكَ: i.e. in breaking the covenant, because they had covenanted with him ﷺ that they would not fight him; i.e. if they do this, فَقَدْ خانُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ قَبْلُ, i.e. they betrayed His allies, the believers, at the outset. The plural of خيانة is خيائن, though it ought to have been said خوائن because it is from the wāw-roots, except that they distinguished between it and the plural of خائنة. One says خائن, خون, خونة and خانة.
